tr.td: Tremor of the writing hand for six months, with shaky, effortful handwriting and spilling from cups; under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem echoing, without asserting, the shaky signatures on his 1616 will (CLM-0006, R); superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Essential tremor (MDS 1608 criteria): bilateral upper-limb postural and kinetic tremor, right more than left, for at least three years, worse over six months, without head or voice tremor or other neurological signs; enhanced by alcohol rebound and caffeine; thyroid and metabolic causes excluded

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. The shakiness of his signatures is documented as an interpretation (CLM-0006, R, possible); no tremor is documented in his lifetime, and the mercury hypothesis (CLM-0010) is disputed.
Hazardous drinking (AUDIT 12; about 24 standard drinks a week with heavier evenings with friends), without an alcohol use disorder; raised GGT
S — Synthetic finding. The only historical mention of his drinking is a story written down decades after his death (CLM-0008, R); it is not treated as evidence of his habits.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with a low-grade fever, one week after starting propranolol; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; it does not assert anything about the fever in John Ward's later story (CLM-0008, R).

tr.td: Primary care visit for six months of tremor of the writing hand in a writer of 51
Two-week review of tremor tests, diagnosis, alcohol follow-up, and movement disorders neurology consultation
Four-week review of propranolol: tremor rating, pulse and blood pressure, drinking, and occupational therapy
Eight-week review: tremor and writing, propranolol at 80 mg, liver tests, and drinking
Same-day sick visit for a cold one week after starting propranolol

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Tremor history and examination with the MDS 1608 classification (rest, postural, and kinetic tremor; distribution; parkinsonism, dystonia, ataxia); TSH, metabolic panel, liver tests, and blood count; a medication, caffeine, and alcohol review
Movement disorders neurology consultation to confirm the tremor type, exclude early Parkinson disease, and advise on treatment

Alcohol: AUDIT screening and a brief intervention (feedback, advice, and a goal of no more than 14 drinks a week and 4 on any day); follow-up of drinking at each visit and GGT after eight to ten weeks
Handwriting sample and Archimedes spiral at each visit; cut coffee to two cups a day, none after midday
Propranolol extended-release 60 mg each morning, increased by response to 80 mg; pulse and blood pressure at each visit; primidone if propranolol fails or is not tolerated
Occupational therapy for writing: weighted and wide-grip pens, posture and forearm support, slower larger script, and dictation software for long drafts
Goals-of-care and advance care planning conversation: a named health care agent and a written directive, alongside the will he is preparing
Classify the tremor and exclude treatable causes by the second visit
Essential tremor diagnosed; TSH, glucose, calcium, and kidney tests normal; no parkinsonism
Legible handwriting for a full page and a steady signature
TETRAS writing item from 3 to 1.5 and the spiral much steadier on propranolol 80 mg with a weighted pen
No more than 14 standard drinks a week and no more than 4 on any day
Within the limits for ten weeks, about 10 drinks a week for the last five; GGT 84 to 49 U/L
Resting pulse above 55 without dizziness, wheeze, or fatigue on propranolol
Pulse 62 and blood pressure 120/76 mmHg on 80 mg, without side effects
